wv_3_rico_suave_buttress.blurb: A tall, blocky buttress on the Kaymoor rim of the New River Gorge, with lines up several of its faces rather than a single wall. About twenty roped climbs mix bolted and gear-protected routes on sandstone, starting around 5.7 and running well into the 5.12s, with a smaller group near 5.13. The core of the grade range is 5.11 to 5.12, so strong leaders have the most to do, while a few easier lines give a warm-up. Kaymoor as a whole is a shady, north-facing rim that stays damp after rain.

wv_7_seven_eleven_wall.blurb: A sandstone wall at Kaymoor, on the rim of the New River Gorge in southern West Virginia. Around twenty routes, most of them bolted with a smaller group protected by gear, cluster heavily in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a handful of 5.13 lines for the very strong and almost nothing easy. That makes it a good stop for a 5.11 climber looking for a day of steady pulling. The Kaymoor rim faces north, so it tends to be shaded and slow to dry after rain.

wv_carnifex_ferry.blurb: A quiet, little-visited sandstone crag in the Summersville and Gauley River district of the New River Gorge region. Roughly twenty routes split between bolted lines and gear climbs, with grades spread from easy 5.5 terrain up through the 5.12s and a cluster of 5.8 climbs. Slabby faces are part of the mix. The hike in is a long one and ends with a short bushwhack, so expect solitude rather than a roadside crag. Some of the bolts are old, so inspect them carefully before trusting them.

wv_luxury_liner.blurb: A single large sandstone boulder in the East Side section of the Needleseye boulder park near Oak Hill, West Virginia. It stands about 15 feet tall, with steep sections and a big flat wall, and holds around twenty problems. Grades run from V2 to V8, concentrated around V4, with a few V7s for stronger boulderers. It sits closer to the parking lot than any other boulder in the park, only a short walk down a drainage trail, which makes it an easy first or last stop of the day. Trail work in the park is ongoing, so the approach may shift.

wv_coral_area.blurb: A small cluster of boulders tucked below the Tilted Tree zone in Coopers Rock State Forest, in northern West Virginia. Twenty problems from V1 up to V9 spread across several named blocks, with an even spread of moderate V2 to V5 lines and a few harder test pieces. Many of the problems are tall, so bring plenty of pads and a spotter. The walk starts on the Tilted Tree trail and drops down a steep hillside to the main blocks. Avoid climbing on wet rock, particularly the footholds.

wv_06_head_wall.blurb: A sector of Bubba City on the north side of the New River Gorge in West Virginia, set off to the west of the central crags. The cliff is a pale and orange sandstone wall regarded as having some of the finest stone in the area. About twenty routes, mostly bolted with a few traditional lines, are packed into the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with 5.11 the most common grade and a couple of 5.13s at the top. Good for strong sport climbers who do not mind a walk in from the central crags.

wv_death_block_area.blurb: A group of three main boulders in the Tilted Tree section of Coopers Rock State Forest, in northern West Virginia, reached by walking west on the foot trails from the Tilted Tree tiers. The boulders mostly face south. The twenty problems range from very easy to the V7 range, with the largest group at V2 or below and a few hard classics for strong climbers. One boulder has moderates, another has easier, less-travelled lines. Stay off wet rock and brush off tick marks after your attempts.
